title: admission-orchestration-tokenbucket-gpu-signals-playbook
summary: Working playbook for orchestrating admission decisions across multi-region clusters using a token-bucket primary limiter augmented by queue-depth and GPU utilization signals. Focused on safe graceful degradation and low-latency routing policies.
body:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures a concrete, implementable playbook for request admission across Redwood’s serving fabric. It focuses on: token-bucket quota enforcement, queue-depth backpressure, and GPU-utilization-driven dynamic throttles. Target is predictable latency under strain, graceful fallbacks to lower-cost/pool variants, and clear control-plane observability for operators.

Assumptions:
- Each request maps to a routing key (customer, route, model, priority).
- Serving nodes expose per-GPU util metrics (gpu_util pct), queue_depth, inflight_tokens (active prefixes cached), and local token-bucket state.
- Control plane can: read aggregated signals, mutate per-route token rates, and instruct route-level fallbacks.
- Multi-region: requests prefer region-local, can failover to secondary regions when capacity/latency policies permit.

High-level policy overview:
1) Per-route token bucket (global logical bucket): primary admission controller keeps a logical token rate (tokens/sec) per (customer, route, model, priority). Tokens represent allowed cost units (approx tokens emitted by model).
2) Node-level fast path: when a node receives a request it first checks local token allowance (fast local cache of global bucket). If tokens available, proceed to enqueue/execute. If not, consult soft-queue and queue-depth rules.
3) Queue-depth backpressure: each worker has a per-GPU queue depth soft cap and hard cap. Soft cap triggers queuing with expected latency bump; hard cap denies.
4) GPU-util throttling multiplier: when average gpu_util > util_high (e.g., 85%), the effective token consumption multiplier increases (simulate slower processing) and token refill is slowed for that region/pool. This reduces new work directed to saturated hardware.
5) Multi-region routing: control plane maintains region capacity score = f(available_tokens, avg_latency, infra_health, gpu_util). Requests are routed by policy (latency-first, cost-first, compliance-first).

Signals and thresholds (initial suggestions):
- token_bucket_rate: per-route baseline rate calibrated from historical throughput and SLO.
- token_bucket_burst: allow short bursts (2x-5x) for spiky traffic.
- node_queue_soft_depth: 6 requests/GPU. node_queue_hard_depth: 12 requests/GPU.
- gpu_util_high: 85% (begin applying multiplier). gpu_util_critical: 95% (aggressive rate cut + immediate spill).
- slow_latency_threshold: request tail > 2x p99 target -> mark node as "degraded".

Admission decision flow (per-request):
1) Resolve routing key and assigned route policy (e.g., customer A, model-small, priority=standard).
2) Consult region preference list (local -> alt1 -> alt2) based on SLO and data residency.
3) For candidate region/pool: check aggregated token balance for route. If tokens available, acquire N tokens (estimated token cost of request).
4) If local node token cache lacks tokens, attempt borrow from region controller within bounded latency (<= 5ms path). If borrow successful, accept and enqueue.
5) If borrow fails, examine queue depth. If queue_depth < soft cap, enqueue with a "queued" admission label and provide client advisory (approx queue wait). If >= hard cap, reject with standardized 429 and offer fallback options.
6) If GPU util in pool > gpu_util_high, apply multiplier M = 1 + (gpu_util - gpu_util_high)/15 (capped at 2.0). This increases token cost and reduces effective tokens, making admission harder.

Fallback strategies (ordered):
- Local cheaper variant: route to smaller quantized model that approximates the response.
- Delay & retry: return fast advisory with retry-after (use only for non-interactive requests).
- Cross-region failover: if policy permits and latency budget allows, route to alternative region.
- Partial responses / truncated completion: for generation tasks, return shorter token budgets.

Control plane responsibilities:
- Maintain authoritative per-route token state, reconcile node caches periodically (every 1–5s).
- Provide APIs for operators to adjust token rates and queue caps live (feature flags).
- Expose region capacity scoring and suggested spill percentages.
- Orchestrate orchestrated fallbacks (canary toggles to switch fallback model families per customer).

Node-level implementation notes:
- Keep admission fast path inline and non-blocking. Use atomic counters for local token cache and queue_depth.
- Local cache TTL short (1s) to reduce divergence but avoid per-request RTT to control plane.
- Use leaky-bucket for queue draining: prefer older requests first unless priority indicates otherwise.
- Emit structured logs/traces for denied requests including reason (TOKEN, QUEUE, GPU_UTIL) and metrics.

Pseudocode (simplified):

accept_request(req):
  route = resolve(req)
  region_candidates = choose_regions(route.policy)
  for region in region_candidates:
    node = pick_node(region)
    if node.local_tokens.try_acquire(req.estimated_cost):
      enqueue(node, req)
      return ACCEPTED
    else:
      if node.queue_depth < SOFT_CAP:
        enqueue_with_label(node, req, "QUEUED_SOFT")
        return ACCEPTED_QUEUED
      elif node.queue_depth >= HARD_CAP:
        continue  // try next region or fallback
  return REJECT(429, reason="capacity")

GPU multiplier sketch used at token accounting:
  effective_cost = base_cost * (1 + max(0, (gpu_util - gpu_util_high))/15)

Observability and SLOs to track:
- token_acquire_latency (control plane sync time).
- admit_rate / reject_rate by reason.
- avg_queue_wait and queue_depth distribution per-gpu.
- p50/p95/p99 latency pre/post admission.
- cross-region spill percentage and additional latency introduced.
- gpu_util trends and correlation with tail latency.
- model_quality drift on fallback models (track evals per-fallback).

Operational runbooks (quick):
- spike detection: if cluster reject_rate > 1% sustained for 5m, increase global burst allowance by +20% (temporary) and open incident.
- sustained high gpu_util: if region gpu_util > gpu_util_critical for > 3m, immediately stop new accepts and trigger cross-region spill for high-priority traffic only.
- rollback fallback change: use route-level feature toggle to revert to primary model within seconds.

Experiment plan (A/B):
- Start with token-bucket-only baseline (current) vs token-bucket + gpu-multiplier. Measure p99 latency, reject_rate, cost-per-token for 2 weeks.
- Canary rollout: enable on 5% of traffic in one region, monitor metrics and error budgets, then expand.

Open questions / risks:
- Token granularity: per-token (fine-grained) vs per-request estimated-cost (coarse). Coarse is cheaper but may mis-estimate long generation calls.
- Borrow latency: bounded borrowing adds complexity and possible increased admission latency—need perf budget.
- Cross-region legal/data constraints: not all traffic may spill; need per-customer flags.
- Model quality on fallback: must instrument user-visible regressions and rollback automation.

Next steps / action items:
- [INF-1345] implement gpu_util multiplier in control plane accounting (Jonah).
- Add structured deny reason to runtime logs and log->metrics pipeline (Priya).
- Run scale test with synthetic burst (Ethan) to validate queue caps.
- Draft customer-facing guidance for failover behavior and 429 semantics (Imani).

Notes & references:
- Prior notes on bucket sizing in internal doc: see confluence link above.
- Related tickets: node admission playbook (existing), capacity-aware routing RFC (under review).

This doc is intentionally pragmatic: start with conservative thresholds, instrument heavily, and iterate quickly by measuring downstream effects on latency, cost, and user-visible quality.

(End of playbook)
